title: Physics and defense technology
competency: Explain how radar, missiles and infrared night vision use physics.

keywords.def: RAdio Detection And Ranging: finding objects by the echoes of radio waves.
Electromagnetic radiation just beyond red light, given off by warm objects.

en.text: Radar sends out radio waves and times the echo. The wave goes to the target and back, so 2R = ct and the range is R = ct/2. A ballistic missile is powered only at the start and then follows a projectile path; a cruise missile is powered all the way. Infrared night vision shows warm objects as bright, because hotter objects give off more infrared.

screens.title: Echo timing
screens.ask: A radar pulse returns 0.0002 s after it was sent. The plane is
screens.after:
The pulse goes to the plane and back.
Total path = 3 × 10⁸ m/s × 0.0002 s = 60 000 m = 60 km.
Half of that is the distance: 30 km.
The trap is 60 km: it forgets the return trip.

screens.title: Radar
paras: RADAR means RAdio Detection And Ranging.
A transmitter sends a signal; the target reflects an echo back to the receiver.
The signal travels 2R in time t at speed c. So 2R = ct and R = ct/2.

screens.title: Radar range
screens.ask: Move the echo time. See the range.
screens.note: R = ct/2. The 2 is because the wave goes there and back.

screens.title: Worked example: radar range
steps: Given: echo time t = 0.8 ms = 8 × 10⁻⁴ s, c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
Formula: R = ct/2 (the pulse goes there and back).

screens.title: Missiles and night vision
paras: Ballistic missiles are rocket-powered only at the start. Then gravity curves their path into an arc.
Cruise missiles are jet-powered all the way.
All objects give off infrared; hotter objects give off more. Night-vision devices show hotter objects brighter.

screens.title: Physics in defence
items: Rocket only at the start. Then gravity alone curves its path into an arc.
Jet-powered all the way. It flies like a small aircraft.
Detects infrared. Warmer objects give off more, so they look brighter.

screens.title: Key words
defs: RAdio Detection And Ranging: finding objects by the echoes of radio waves.
Electromagnetic radiation just beyond red light, given off by warm objects.

screens.text: Radar range formula: why is the range R = ct/2 and not ct?
opts: The wave goes to the target and back
screens.ans: The wave goes to the target and back
screens.why:
The pulse travels to the target.
The echo travels the same distance back.
So the total path is ct = 2R.
Divide by 2: R = ct/2.
Trap: radio waves do not travel at c/2; they travel at c.

screens.ask: Radar range: an echo returns after 1.0 ms. The target is ___ km away
screens.why:
Formula: R = ct/2.
Convert: t = 1.0 ms = 1.0 × 10⁻³ s.
Substitute: R = (3 × 10⁸ m/s × 1.0 × 10⁻³ s)/2 = 1.5 × 10⁵ m.
Change to km: 1.5 × 10⁵ m = 150 km.
Trap: forgetting ÷2 gives 300 km.
screens.clue: Use R = ct/2, then change m to km.

screens.text: Kinds of missile: a missile that is powered only at the start, then follows an arc, is
screens.why:
A ballistic missile burns its rocket only at launch.
After that only gravity acts on it (Newtonian mechanics).
So it follows a curved, projectile-like arc.
A cruise missile is jet-powered all the way.
screens.clue: Which one is powered all the way?

screens.text: Infrared night vision: a person at night looks
screens.why:
All objects give off infrared.
Hotter objects give off more infrared.
A person (about 37 °C) is warmer than the cool ground.
So the person looks brighter on the screen.

screens.text: Waves in defence, true or false: radar and night vision both use electromagnetic waves.
screens.why:
Radar uses radio waves or microwaves.
Night vision detects infrared.
Both are parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.
So the statement is true.

screens.ask: Radar echo time: a target is 45 km away. The echo returns after ___ microseconds
screens.why:
Rearrange R = ct/2: t = 2R/c.
Convert: R = 45 km = 45 000 m.
Substitute: t = 2 × 45 000 / (3 × 10⁸) = 3 × 10⁻⁴ s.
Change to μs: 3 × 10⁻⁴ s = 300 μs.
Check: R = 3 × 10⁸ × 3 × 10⁻⁴ / 2 = 45 000 m ✓

items.ask: Discussion question, radar range: the echo returns after 200 μs. Range = ___ km
items.why:
Formula: R = ct/2.
Convert: t = 200 μs = 2 × 10⁻⁴ s.
Substitute: R = (3 × 10⁸ × 2 × 10⁻⁴)/2 = 3 × 10⁴ m.
Change to km: 30 km.

items.text: Discussion question 1.8: which physics is used in radar and night vision? Pick all that apply.
items.why:
Both use electromagnetic waves.
Radar works by reflection: the echo.
Night vision detects infrared given off by warm bodies.
Pascal's principle is about pressure in fluids, so it is not used.

test.ask: Radar range: the echo returns after 0.4 ms. Range = ___ km
test.why:
Formula: R = ct/2.
Convert: t = 0.4 ms = 4 × 10⁻⁴ s.
R = (3 × 10⁸ × 4 × 10⁻⁴)/2 = 6 × 10⁴ m.
Result: 60 km.
Trap: without ÷2 you get 120 km.

RA = RAdio, D = Detection, A = And, R = Ranging.
It finds objects (detection) and their distance (ranging) with radio echoes.

test.text: Kinds of missile: a cruise missile is
test.why:
A cruise missile has a jet engine that runs all the way.
A ballistic missile is powered only at launch.
Answer: jet-powered all the way.

test.text: Infrared night vision: night-vision images show
test.why:
Night-vision devices detect infrared.
Hotter objects give off more infrared.
So brightness on the screen shows temperature differences.

test.ask: Radar echo time: range 75 km. Echo time = ___ μs
test.why:
Formula: t = 2R/c.
Convert: R = 75 km = 7.5 × 10⁴ m.
t = 2 × 7.5 × 10⁴ / (3 × 10⁸) = 5 × 10⁻⁴ s.
Result: 500 μs.

notes.text: p.19 says infrared output is "proportional to temperature"; it rises much faster (∝ T⁴ for a black body). Lessons say "hotter gives off more".
p.18: missile thrust is produced because momentum is conserved (Newton's third law), not altered "to conserve momentum".
Missile content is kept to the book's physics (powered vs. ballistic paths); no design detail is added.
